title: Test standard per-project config
description: Where a repository states its own numbers. The standard carries rules; every value that is specific to one codebase lives here. Place at .claude/tests.config.json. Anything omitted falls back to the standard's default, and a repository with no file at all is audited against defaults.

tiers.description: The execution tiers and the globs that decide membership. The rule is that the filename declares the tier, so these globs must partition the test set: no file in two tiers, none in neither.

excluded.description: Test files the standard does not govern — an environment-gated integration suite is the usual case. Naming them here is what keeps them from being audited as violations.

coverage.description: Two mechanisms, and each is blind to the other's case. The ratchet catches slow erosion; the floor catches a collapse the ratchet would tolerate if it were ever loosened.

uncoveredLineCap.description: The ratchet: the most uncovered lines the repository tolerates. Derived from a measured run, never chosen. Lowering it is the only sanctioned edit.

floorPercent.description: The absolute floor. Not a target — the number below which the suite stops meaning anything. Meaningless on its own: tests that execute code and assert nothing satisfy it, which is why it is paired with a mutation bar.

perPath.description: A tighter cap for a path that earns one — a pure calculation core is the usual case. Per-path entries do not inherit the global set.

mutation.description: The only mechanical check that a covered line is asserted on, and what stops the coverage floor from being decoration.

target.description: Globs the mutation run covers. Narrow on purpose: the run costs minutes per module, and a pure calculation core is where a survivor means a real defect rather than an equivalent mutant.

maxSurvivingPercent.description: The bar. Deliberately harder than the published orientation, because a coverage floor it is paired with is satisfiable by tests that assert nothing. Two things make it work rather than tune: an equivalent mutant cannot be killed by any test and must be annotated one at a time, and an uncovered line produces a survivor for free.

breakBuild.description: Whether a score below the bar fails a run. Leave false until a real score exists — the first score is a measurement, not a verdict.

rule.description: The rule number from the standard's canonical table.

waitsOn.description: What has to exist before the rule can be met. A task id, a path, a sentence — whatever the repository can point at.

interim.description: What a test author does in the meantime. An interim written down is a decision; the same code with no interim is a violation nobody authorised.

blockedRules.description: Rules this repository cannot meet yet. The auditor does not report a blocked rule's violations as findings — it reports the block once. An entry with no `waitsOn` is a rule quietly abandoned, which is why the field is required.

timeBudgetMs.description: Per-tier budget for a single case, keyed by tier name. Reported, never failed: the number moves with the machine, and a budget that fails a build gets tuned into uselessness on the first slow runner.

environment.description: The runner's environment for this tier.

setupFile.description: This tier's setup file. Keep it small: a setup file that imports a module which instantiates the transport graph at load defeats every per-file substitution in the tier.
